codes.name: Sustain cooperation
codes.definition: Keeps or restores a stable high-price or tied arrangement because it is working and is worth preserving, or because no deviation would pay. No threat is named.

codes.name: Fear of price war or retaliation
codes.definition: Holds back from raising or cutting because it fears the rival would retaliate, or that a price war or collapse of cooperation would follow.

codes.name: Play safe, avoid losing sales
codes.definition: Picks a safe price to protect against earning zero or losing all buyers (for example being undercut). The stress is on downside protection, not on the rival's retaliation.

codes.name: Match or follow the rival
codes.definition: Sets its price equal to the rival's current or expected price, including copying the rival after the rival undercut or moved.

codes.name: Undercut to win the market
codes.definition: Cuts price below the rival's current or expected price to take all buyers and earn a larger immediate profit.

codes.name: Infer rival's pattern from history
codes.definition: Reasons from the rival's observed past behaviour (steady, mirroring, alternating, drifting) to predict what it will do next.

codes.name: Probe the rival with a raise
codes.definition: Raises or changes price on purpose as an experiment, to see whether the rival follows, cooperates or punishes.

codes.name: Recover after a failed move
codes.definition: Returns to the earlier price after its own raise or cut was undercut, punished or earned nothing, to restore cooperation or profit.

codes.name: Raise to a higher shared price
codes.definition: Moves to a higher joint price because ties there pay more, or to escape a low-price trap.

codes.name: Compare immediate profits
codes.definition: Chooses by explicitly computing and comparing the immediate profit of options, without citing cooperation, retaliation or the rival's pattern.

codes.name: other
codes.definition: Reasons that fit none of the above (including any talk of the game ending).
